Subject: MSA: IP liability and allocation - Redwood / Variform

Lindsey / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the IP/third-party claim discussion so we have a shared plan heading into the redline exchange.

Summary of Variform asks:
- Full customer indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to customer use of output (customer-sourced prompts/data).
- Escrow/holdback mechanism triggered by claim notice above $250k (customer wants lower threshold).
- Defense-control reservation (customer wants approval rights over counsel selection for certain claims).

Where Redwood stands (high-level):
- We can offer limited defend-and-reimburse for direct infringement of models we host, with a liability cap tied to the order form.
- We want to preserve right to select counsel for technical defense; we can consider a mutual consent window for customer-designated counsel in material litigation.
- Escrow is negotiable but needs a practical threshold and trigger language (insurance offsets/subrogation need to be clear).

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly/Legal: suggest a defensible fallback redline (one-pager of our preferred language + a compromise ladder).
2) Redwood Commercial (Ben + me): prepare the commercial concession ladder (credits / ordering/ term adjustments tied to cap changes).
3) Variform: please send your redlined MSA (we saw a draft last week; attach final redlines).

Attachments: Variform_MSARedlines_20290722.pdf (we'll review) and a short escrow proposal our ops team pulled together.

Callout: this thread will be our single source for comments; Kimberly, can you put a short fallback language in by EOD? Ben — I'll coordinate a commercial impact estimate after Kimberly's draft.

Thanks,

Sean Gallagher

Subject: Re: MSA: IP liability and allocation - Redwood / Variform

Sean / team — looping in a short legal position and compromise ladder. High level points below; I attached proposed fallback language (short paragraph style) to the working doc.

Key legal posture (short):
- Redwood will defend and indemnify for third-party claims alleging infringement caused by Redwood-provided models or code (i.e., not Customer-provided prompts or datasets).
- If the claim arises from Customer data or prompts, we propose mutual indemnity: customer defends/indemnifies for claims attributable to their input; Redwood will offer limited remediation support.
- Defense control: Redwood retains initial right to select counsel for technical infringement claims but will permit customer to propose outside counsel if there is a conflict or reasonable cause; any customer-selected counsel must be subject to our normal conflicts check and fee guidelines.
- Caps & escrow: propose an order-form-specific cap (e.g., 6 months of SaaS fees) and an escrow threshold at $500k with insurance offset and subrogation carve-out. Customer wants lower threshold — commercial to advise on acceptability.

Open questions I need from commercial to complete redline by EOD:
- Acceptable cap band (months of revenue or flat-dollar).
- Whether we're prepared to accept customer counsel consent rights for claims exceeding X (commercial to propose X).

I recommend we include a discrete evidence-preservation obligation for both parties (short checklist) and a notice window of no less than 30 days for potential claims.

I'll attach: "Kimberly_Fallback_Clause_20290723.docx" to the working Drive link and will mark the redline with inline rationale.

-Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: MSA: IP liability and allocation - Redwood / Variform

Kimberly — this looks good. Commercial considerations: Variform has tagged this as a must-have for procurement. Lowering the escrow trigger to $250k materially increases revenue risk; if legal wants that, we should ask for a 10% order increase or a 6-month credit protection in exchange.

Proposed concession ladder (commercial):
- Base: Order-form cap = 6 months ARR; escrow threshold = $500k; Redwood selects counsel.
- Concession 1: Escrow threshold = $350k -> customer receives a 5% rebate on first-year fees.
- Concession 2: Escrow threshold = $250k -> customer receives 10% rebate + extended SLA window (2x credits).

Also recommend we offer a limited carveout where customer can request independent counsel only for non-technical claims; for technical/engineer-driven defenses Redwood retains lead counsel.

If Variform insists on broad counsel consent, that's a hard ask — legal should flag any regulatory/client-side exposure.

I'll draft a short commercial memo for execs tying each concession to P&L impact.

-Ben
Head of Sales, Enterprise

Subject: Re: MSA: IP liability and allocation - Redwood / Variform

Thanks, Sean — appreciate the clear recap. We circulated your positions to procurement/legal and attached our redlined MSA for clarity. High-level responses to your points: 

- Variform position: we need the ability to require an escrow hold starting at $250k (our risk team insists).
- Counsel: for claims that may materially impact our public customers we need the option to nominate counsel; we would agree to a short mutual-consent process but need teeth (e.g., ability to escalate to mediation if counsel consent stalls).
- Cap: we are generally comfortable with an order-form cap but would like the cap to be at least 12 months of SaaS fees for mission-critical products.

We can be flexible if Redwood offers: (i) a commensurate discount/credit or (ii) an expanded insurance requirement (higher minimum limits).

Attached: Variform_MSARedlines_20290722.pdf (redlines inline) and Evidence_Request_List.xlsx (list of documents Variform's legal team will request in case of a claim).

Proposed next step: please provide Kimberly's fallback redline + commercial uplift proposal by EOD so we can see a concrete trade. If possible, schedule 30-minute call tomorrow to close open items.

-Lindsey Cole
